subject: scatter plot between columns in a dataframe?

messages.author: 6cb19f1966a6962b
messages.subject: scatter plot between columns in a dataframe?
parts:
Hi,

I have a data.frame of 4 Variables. Lets call them x1 x2...x4

I want to do a scatter plot  between x1 and all other variables x2, x3 ... x4 (but not with itself i.e. x1). Then just show correlation values on the plot.

d <- data.frame(x1=rnorm(10), x2=rnorm(10),  x3=rnorm(10),x4=rnorm(10))

How can we do that?
Thanks,
Bick

d <- data.frame(x1=rnorm(10), x2=rnorm(10),  x3=rnorm(10),x4=rnorm(10))
rethinking::pairs(d)

messages.author: d567d0ef3c054a35
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: scatter plot between columns in a dataframe?
parts:
The appended is my attempt at this using the Hadley stuff.  The two calls to ggplot produce the same output, so either would be sufficient.  Also, the `gather` call removes x1.

-- Mike

library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

df <- data.frame(x1=rnorm(10), x2=rnorm(10),  x3=rnorm(10), x4=rnorm(10))

df %>% gather(-x1, key="var", value="val") %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = val, y=x1, color=var)) +
    geom_point() +
    facet_wrap(~ var, nrow=3)

df %>% gather(-x1, key="var", value="val") %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = val, y=x1, color=var)) +
    geom_point() +
    facet_grid(var ~ .)

messages.subject: Re: scatter plot between columns in a dataframe?
parts: To do what Mike suggested in base R:
d <- data.frame(x1=rnorm(10), x2=rnorm(10),  x3=rnorm(10),x4=rnorm(10))

# Using column index
par(mfrow = c(1,3))
sapply(2:4, function(i) plot(d[,1] ~ d[,i]))

# Or using the column names
vars = c("x2","x3","x4")
sapply(vars, function(x) plot(d[,"x1"] ~ d[,x])

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Re: scatter plot between columns in a dataframe?
parts:
Thanks, Matt. I was curious about that myself and had constructed
essentially the same solution as yours but was too busy to post it
yesterday. I've appended my version, which would seem to be
unnecessary, given your clean solution, but I want to make a couple of
points about the general subject.

(1) To make a scatterplot of two columns of a data frame is dead
simple in base graphics:

plot(foo$x1, foo$x3) ## or equivalent indexing "foo[["x1"]], etc.

To the best of my knowledge (correct me if I'm wrong), doing this via
ggplot requires an initial step that changes the format of the data
frame from the (natural) wide format to the long format. This is what
the "gather" step does in the solution I posted. This seems, umm,
baroque to me.

(2) OTOH, I tried to "gussy up" the base-graphics solution to make it
a reasonable facsimile of the ggplot solution. This required the use
of a bit of mildly-arcane, graphics voodoo. (Could you guess what
"mgp" does without looking it up?)

So this seems to be the tradeoff: seemingly-gratuitous data fiddling
with ggplot or seemingly-gratuitous fiddling with graphics parameters
with base graphics.

Chacun à son goût.

-- Mike


df1 <- data.frame(x1=rnorm(10), x2=rnorm(10), x3=rnorm(10), x4=rnorm(10))

par(mfrow=c(length(df1) - 1, 1))
par(mgp=c(1.8, 0.5, 0))
plot_colors <- 1:length(df1)
names(plot_colors) <- names(df1)

foo <- sapply(names(df1), function(nxn) {
if (nxn != "x1") {
plot(df1[["x1"]], df1[[nxn]],
xlab=nxn, ylab="x1",
main=paste("x1 vs. ", nxn),
cex.lab=1.5,
cex.main=2.0,
xlim=c(-3.5, 3.5),
ylim=c(-3.5, 3.5),
pch=20,
cex=1.5,
col=plot_colors[nxn])
}
})
